Subject: Re: [ydn-delicious] Instead of 503, repeating API /posts/all gives 200 but no posts.  Eeek!

I'm replying to the same thread because, although I have not isolated  
the "no posts" problem yet, I saw a similar problem today.

In one of my del.icio.us test accounts, I had 576 posts.  Over a  
period of about 30 minutes, and in about 5 batches of 10-50 each, I  
deleted 99 posts, using my app, which sends https://api.del.icio.us/v1/posts/delete 
  After each batch, I would wait a few minutes and send https://api.del.icio.us/v1/posts/all 
, but in all cases posts/all.  But in all cases I got all 576 posts,  
including the ones that had been deleted.

I loaded my account's del.icio.us in Safari and it showed the correct  
answer, that I had only 477 posts.  (Yes, I was logged in with the  
correct account so I was seeing all posts, even those not shared.)

I then sent posts/all with curl to various different del.icio.us  
servers as suggested by Toby and got the following results:

curl to https://api.del.icio.us/v1/posts/all
Result: 576 posts (wrong)

Wait a few minutes
curl to https://s19.del.re4.yahoo.net/v1/posts/all
Result: 477 posts (correct)

Wait a few minutes
curl to https://s46.del.re4.yahoo.net/v1/posts/all
Result: 477 posts (correct)

Wait a few minutes
curl to https://fe03.del.re4.yahoo.net/v1/posts/all
Result: 477 posts (correct)

Wait a few minutes
https://fe06.del.re4.yahoo.net/v1/posts/all
Result: 477 posts (correct)

Wait a few minutes
Use my application to https://api.del.icio.us/v1/posts/all
Result: 477 posts (correct)

I tried to reproduce this twice using a smaller account that had only  
a few posts, but the smaller account worked correctly; posts/all  
immediately reflected a deletion of 1 post.

I then repeated the process on this larger account, deleting 12 posts,  
then 1 post, then 12 posts.  But it's working fine now; in all three  
cases sending posts/all to the regular del.icio.us server gave me the  
correct answer after a minute.  (I don't send posts/all immediately  
for fear of being locked out for 3 hours.)

I do use a local cache and understand that posts/all should be rarely  
used in practice, but it is needed to re-sync after posts/update  
indicates behind-the-back changes, or manually after power failures or  
network outages.

I don't see any lag times documented in del.icio.us./help/api.  Is  
there anything workaround I can use to get more reliable results?   
Since I'm not sure if my app is working yet, I spend a couple extra  
hours debugging when stuff like this happens :( Are there possibly  
certain times of the day or week when servers can get out of sync?

Thanks,

Jerry Krinock

On 2007 Oct, 08, at 10:56, Toby Elliott wrote:

> Thanks for letting us know about this. That's quite alarming, though
> it doesn't seem to have been endemic.
>
> There are three things to try if it happens again that will help us
> debug the issue:
>
> 1) Try accessing posts/all at the following hosts:
>
> https://s19.del.re4.yahoo.net
> https://s46.del.re4.yahoo.net
> https://fe03.del.re4.yahoo.net
> https://fe06.del.re4.yahoo.net
>
> (you'll need to disable certificate checking in curl to do it)
>
> This'll let us know if one of the clusters is having problems.
>
> 2) Try accessing it from a web browser rather than curl, just in case
> there's a problem with the authentication.
>
> 3) Try saving an item in your account. There shouldn't be any caching
> going on, but if there is, it should reset it.
>
> Hopefully that'll help us figure out what could be going wrong here.
>
> Regards,
> Toby Elliott
> del.icio.us
>
>
